events.title: Windows PowerShell 1.0 released
events.summary: Microsoft released Windows PowerShell 1.0 on November 14, 2006 at ITForum — a .NET-based shell and scripting language for Windows administration.
events.about: PowerShell pipes objects, not just text — `Get-Process`, `Where-Object`, and modules automate Active Directory, Azure, and Exchange at scale. Admins and DevOps teams script deployments, audit configs, and manage cloud resources. It later became cross-platform as PowerShell Core.

narrative.whyChosen: PowerShell replaced fragile CMD/batch scripting with a consistent object pipeline on Windows.
narrative.whyImportant: It made .NET APIs directly scriptable and became the backbone of Microsoft server automation.
narrative.problemSolved: Windows lacked a modern composable shell; admins glued together VBScript, WMI, and one-off binaries.
